answer: Save the progress point at the lowest offset not yet written: the position just below the first gap in the completed sequence (source: pa_pattern_backpressure_scaling.md, the commit-offset passage after the 9,500-record pause). Because the 10 threads finish out of order, anything above that point may already be done, and that is fine: a crash replays work, so nothing is lost. If you save the highest finished position instead, any offset still in flight below it is skipped on restart and never reprocessed, so those records are lost silently. Saving the highest position trades that loss for speed, not the other way round.
